moat_against: ROIC history is weak and volatile: roic_proxy -0.66% / 0.52% / 5.74% / 0.75% / 13.21% over FY2021-25 — no through-cycle record above the cost of capital
Medtronic (Solitaire) and Stryker (Trevo) lead neurovascular thrombectomy with far larger scale, distribution and R&D breadth; Johnson & Johnson also competes
Revenue concentrated in thrombectomy — a single-category bet exposed to competing technologies and procedure trends
Reimbursement/payback pressure (Italian government payback provision hit FY2024 revenue) and heavy SBC ($59.5M TTM) dilute the economics
moat_for: World's leading thrombectomy company — pure-play focus on aspiration/CAVT (computer-assisted vacuum thrombectomy) across neuro, venous, pulmonary and arterial clots
Proprietary CAVT technology and IP portfolio, validated by clinical data (STORM-PE randomized trial; STRIKE-PE registry)
Physician training, clinical workflow integration and installed pump base create real switching costs; single-use disposables give recurring procedure-linked revenue
Gross margin 67.1% in FY2025 and 67.9% in Q2 2026, up from 63.2% in FY2024 — pricing/mix power
moat_justification: Leading pure-play thrombectomy franchise (CAVT computer-assisted vacuum technology, proprietary IP, physician training and workflow switching costs, 67-68% gross margins), but ROIC has not stayed above the cost of capital through a cycle — roic_proxy was -0.66% (2021), 0.52% (2022), 5.74% (2023), 0.75% (2024, impairment year) and only reached 13.21% in 2025 — and Medtronic/Stryker compete with far larger scale and distribution. A 7+ would need proven durable high ROIC; the measured history does not show it.
name: Penumbra, Inc
one_liner: Quality thrombectomy leader, moat 5/10 — standalone DCF does not clear 15% at any scenario (weighted IRR 5.1%, IV@15% $57.29 vs $320.86 price; clears 15% only below ~$57); the price is anchored to Boston Scientific's pending $374/share acquisition, not to standalone owner's earnings.
